spec: trustless-ai/deils "leg 2" (Merlini's held-content-behind-commitment design), pinned in Telegram msg_id 1623 (case ownership), 1632/2111-2112 (canonicalization + ref-string format correction). Reference implementation: invinoveritas POST /prove {disclose:false} + POST /prove/{proof_id}/reveal.
ref_format: "sha256:" + 64 lowercase hex. NOT "0x"+hex -- corrected msg_id 2111/2112, matches invinoveritas's own decision_ref convention.
canonicalization: RFC 8785 JCS: recursively sorted object keys, compact separators (no whitespace), raw UTF-8 (not \uXXXX-escaped). Equivalent to Python json.dumps(v, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False).

cases.description: Happy path: revealed content hashes to the published commitment exactly.
Same content, different input key order -- MUST still bind. Proves the shared canonical JSON does the work, not string-equality.
One byte of revealed content changed (artifact_hash's last char) -- MUST be content_commitment_mismatch. Proves the check says NO loudly, no silent pass.
Nothing disclosed yet -- pending, not a failure. No revealed_content is submitted; the checker must not attempt a recompute over unbound content.

Deliberately-wrong-obvious-answer case (Correctover-style, distinct from the top-level near-miss above): keys are shuffled at MULTIPLE NESTED LEVELS, not just the top level. A checker that only sorts top-level keys, or does a raw string diff instead of a recursive JCS canonicalization, would report this as a mismatch (or falsely pass without ever canonicalizing). The correct recursive canonicalization must still bind.
